text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
...
That should do it.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
One day, Air Shakur shows up at my
office with a
large cardboard box.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
It's yours.
Keep what ya want and chuck
whatever you don't.
choice_data_list: Sh-Shakur-san? What on earth is this...?

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
I don't really understand, but I accept it
for now
and then check the contents.
Everything is still
sealed. It seems she
hasn't touched any of it since
it was
delivered.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
The contents are absolute chaos. At
first, I think
it's just crammed full of junk
food, but then I
notice some healthy,
organic food mixed in there
too.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
There are "health drinks" with no
scientific
backing mixed in with the
latest scientific magazines.
I also find
what appears to be a child's towel as
well
 as a stylish handkerchief. Amid this
assortment of
seemingly random items,
something catches my eye.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
It shows a youthful yet frail Umamusume
cradling
a child in what looks to be a
bar. There's a
message on the back of
the photo.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
That's right.
It's all from my mom.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
My curiosity gets the best of me a few
days later,
and Air Shakur lightly
acknowledges it was a gift
from home.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
It's all about what I expected. Man, she's
so
pathetic.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
She just wants to give the appearance of
being a
parent. That's why there's no
rhyme or reason to
what she sent.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
I mean, a kids towel and a baby picture?
I
imagine that's her way of saying she
wants things
to go back to how they
used to be.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
Before I was old enough to know any
better, my
mom dressed me up in
whatever she liked. She
just misses the
days when I went along with
everything
like a good little girl.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
This is not her typical tone. I can gather
from her
open aggression that there's a
deep rift between
her and her mother.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
The message on the back of the
photograph of
the two reads: "At the
very least, tell me what you
want me to
do. Try to understand my feelings."
choice_data_list: (Passing along that message might just add fuel to the fire...)

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
I can't even remember the last time we
spoke
properly. You'd think she'd take
the hint by now
that I'm through with
her.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text: Besides... she was the first to throw in the towel. She should have just ended it there.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
A possible reason for all the random
items strikes
me. She may have no idea
what Air Shakur
actually needs. This
could be the result of her
agonizing over
every possibility.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
"Try to understand my feelings." I
imagine this
might be a plea for not only
understanding, but
for a chance to
speak.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text: But what?
choice_data_list: True, maybe we can't understand it, but...

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
choice_data_list: Still, maybe that's their way of showing they want to do something.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
Yeah, right.
And even if that was the
case, I don't need her
forcing anything
on me.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
Not wanting to intrude any further, I
decide to
change the subject.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
Not wanting to intrude any further, I
decide to
change the subject.
choice_data_list: Where did you take that photo?
Where did you take that photo?
Still, that mountain of cardboard boxes...

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text: Just some bar she used to work at.
choice_data_list: Where did you take that photo?
Where did you take that photo?
Still, that mountain of cardboard boxes...

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
As if she could do that without making a
mess of
everything.
No, she was a singer.
choice_data_list: So your mom was a bartender.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
She sat in the corner and sang for
everyone while
they drank.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
So her mother was a singer. I'm
interested in
hearing more, but Air
Shakur doesn't seem to
want to continue
the discussion.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
I take another look at the photo. Her
mother has
a gentle look about her,
while Air Shakur looks
like she was as
uncompromising as a kid as she is
now.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
All kids look more or less the same at
that age.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
Ah... Just look at that outfit. Freakin' frill
city.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
I hated it so much that I tore it to shreds
one day
when she wasn't around. I
remember her crying
her eyes out after.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
And the way she cried... looking right at
me with
tears streaming down her face...
I couldn't stand
it.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
I wonder if Air Shakur and her mother
will have a
chance to talk sometime in
the future.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
It seems like too much to have come
from just a
package or two. I suspect
that...

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text: Of course not.
choice_data_list: You haven't opened it once since the care packages started coming?

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text: No, hang on. I opened one.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text: Well, Doto did. Not me.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
Yeah. Y'know, same room? Apparently,
she
thought it was for her.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
No idea why, but apparently my mom
sent some
super spicy snacks. Anyway,
Doto wolfed them all
down.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
She practically begged for me to forgive
her when
she realized. She wouldn't stop
moping. Can you
imagine how annoying
it is to deal with that in
your own room?

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
I told her she did me a favor since I
didn't even
want them in the first place,
and I'd give her even
more. That made
her happy. Too happy...

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text:
She started talking to me all the time
after that.

text_block_list.name: Air Shakur
text_block_list.text: Weirdo.

text_block_list.name: Monologue
text_block_list.text:
I imagine scenes like that are not
altogether
uncommon in their dorm
room, and I get the
feeling I've caught a
glimpse of the reason why
Meisho Doto
is so attached to Air Shakur.
